title: Playbook-as-Code transpiler for operator tasklets
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Background: Our oncall and support teams maintain dozens of textual playbooks in Confluence and ad-hoc scripts in Drive. These are hard to keep executable, testable, and safe for non-senior operators. This ticket scopes a small, focused prototype: a Playbook-as-Code transpiler that converts authored support playbooks (YAML/markdown with step annotations) into a verified, idempotent task graph that the operator runtime can execute as a first-class tasklet.

Goals:
- Provide a one-way transpile path from human-authored playbook artifacts into operator task graphs (JSONL task definitions the runtime accepts).
- Embed safety wrappers (preconditions, dry-run, canary flag, single-step rollback markers) automatically to reduce blast radius.
- Produce executable metadata: timeout, retry policy, RBAC scope, audit-log hints, telemetry tag-set.
- Integrate with existing admin utilities so the transpiled tasklets can invoke: secret-safe shelllets, KV cache invalidation, model-rollover scripts, and dashboards.
- Offer a local dry-run simulator and a CI lint stage so authors get fast feedback before rollout.

Non-goals:
- Not implementing a full visual editor. Not supporting arbitrary plugins in v1. Not changing the operator runtime API shape (we will target the existing task ingestion path).

Design notes:
- Input format: extended markdown or YAML with step blocks annotated: "step:id", "guards:", "effects:". We'll provide a minimal schema and a handful of helper macros for common ops patterns.
- Transpiler implementation: lightweight Go binary (playbook-transpile) that outputs task-graph JSONL. Chosen for easy integration into CI and parity with other infra tools.
- Safety model: every mutating step is wrapped with a generated precondition check and a simulated dry-run step. Steps that access secrets must declare a secret token and are emitted as scoped RPC calls to the admin utility service rather than inline shell commands.
- Observability: emit structured spans for each step (op id, playbook id, duration, success/failure, precondition status) and wire to the Console via events API.

Acceptance criteria:
1) The transpiler converts two canonical playbooks (incident-db-rollback, model-cache-warmup) to task-graph artifacts that the runtime can execute without code changes.
2) A guarded mutating step demonstrates rollback on simulated failure in the dry-run harness.
3) Lint stage added to repo CI that rejects playbooks that declare un-scoped secrets or missing guards.
4) Internal SRE team completes two run-throughs with the alpha feature-flagged rollout and accepts usability checklist.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Week 1: schema + prototype transpiler for subset (no-secrets, simple shell commands).
- Week 2: add safety wrappers, dry-run harness, and telemetry emission.
- Week 3: integrate with admin utilities RPC path for secrets and KV ops; add CI linting.
- Week 4: internal alpha + feedback loop, bugfixes, prepare PRs.

Rollout plan:
- Feature-flag under "playbook_transpiler_alpha".
- Alpha enabled for SRE and two oncall pagers.
- After 1 week of internal use and two successful incident replays, flip a broader internal opt-in.
- Post-mortem and checklist before public/documented release.

Risk & mitigations:
- Risk: transpiler introduces veiled behavior changes vs human playbooks. Mitigation: run diff-mode: emit a simulated execution log that shows exact invoked operations; require sign-off before enabling real execution.
- Risk: secrets might leak into logs. Mitigation: enforce secret token use and redact at transpile-time; telemetry schema includes redaction markers.

Links & artifacts: 
- Design doc (working): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Playbook+as+Code+Transpiler
- Prototype repo (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/playbook-transpile/tree/alpha
- CI lint draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-ci/pull/412
- Runtime task ingestion: https://github.com/redwood-inference/operator-runtime/pull/994

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus review on safety wrapper contract and the secret-handling surface.
- Prefer narrow MVP: fewer macros, clearer errors, and stronger linting over broader feature set.
